$description: How App Cloner isolates a copy of an application, read by the Windows and Linux App Cloners; the macOS clone_app.sh keeps its own detection, held to the same executable names by tools/test/test-app-cloner-families.cjs. A source program is matched by its executable's base name, lower-cased and without `.exe`, in `detection_order`; an Electron program is also recognised by a `markers` path next to its real executable. Each family's `arguments` are passed before the user's own item to open; `{profile}` is the clone's private profile folder, `{window_class}` its own window class (so the dock or taskbar groups the clone apart) and `{home}` the user's home folder. An argument with `platforms` is passed only there. `web_app` is the argument that opens a URL as a separate application window. A program of no family (native) gets no argument: on Linux its XDG base directories point into the profile instead; Windows has no per-process equivalent, so its native clone is a separate shortcut only.
